decisions.reason: “Agitation” preserves the voice’s turbulent emotional state; “emotion” is too generic.
SOL keeps the slow, deliberate blink without changing the action.
“Startling” adds an effect absent from the source; “perfect clarity” preserves its emphasis on vivid perception.
The preceding sentence already says this is a first-ever sensation, so SOL removes redundant wording without losing meaning.
“Uniquely” preserves the source’s distinctive manner; “unfailingly” changes that to consistency.
SOL keeps the sunset image and the final flame at life’s darkening edge.
The source explicitly says the thought came to him suddenly; deleting it drops that beat.
SOL preserves both groups of people and the loss, while keeping the recollection natural.
The source says countless emotions; SOL drops that quantity.
SOL’s “them all” naturally refers to the emotions and keeps the sense.
SOL preserves the contrast and the necessity of running toward death without adding “straight.”
“Expression” and “moment” preserve the System notice’s meaning and voice.
SOL keeps the familiar clear chime and its effect on him.
SOL retains the promised light and its death-forgetting brightness.
SOL keeps the body’s trembling stopping as pain and death close in.
“Increases greatly” preserves the substantial temporary increase in Qi Sense.
“Seeped” keeps the warmth entering his back and the spark swelling into flame.
“Sooner or later” preserves the eventual clash and destruction.
“One flame to begin with” naturally conveys their shared root and original unity.
“Shared his qi” preserves the energy given without hesitation.
“Wounds large and small covered his body” keeps the source’s range of injuries.
Naming Jeok Cheongang directly preserves the subject and avoids needless apposition.
SOL makes explicit that he suppresses both the joy and the sorrow.
SOL preserves time starting again and the step forward without changing the sequence.
“My fight alone” keeps the hypothetical solitude and the possibility of giving up.
“Looked back on my life” narrows the source’s reflection on the time he had lived through.
The source describes the earth itself as reddish and heated; SOL changes this to a reddish glow.
“Advanced” carries the group’s movement into the scene without changing who is present.
The civilians are retained in the following sentence, so deleting this separate fragment loses no content.
SOL retains the civilians following like a wave and their shift from desperate cries to calling a name.
“A jolt like lightning” preserves the sudden bodily shiver without implying literal lightning.
SOL keeps both their lack of internal energy and proper weapons, as well as the tools they grip.
SOL preserves the faces flashing through his mind and his charge toward the fanatics.
“My toes” naturally renders the listed point of the foot and keeps the movement sequence.
SOL keeps the instinctive movements and the wind and rain being split.
“Crossed the air” preserves the cutting sound sweeping through the space.
“Slit throats” naturally preserves the fanatics clutching their cut throats as they fall.
SOL drops that the enemies could not react “in time,” a meaningful detail of their failed response.
SOL keeps the next wave’s inability to react as it fills the gaps.
“Kept close” naturally conveys that he always carried the saber on his person.
“Rough appearance” makes explicit the contrast with his character while keeping the source’s sense.
The pronoun still clearly refers to Song Ilseom, and SOL preserves his complaints and where he fought.
“To protect someone” preserves the purpose for which he left the path he had followed.
SOL preserves the speaker’s confidence in the person he knew, using his name for clarity.
“Come to know” weakens the source’s meaningful ties with the two unorthodox faction members.
SOL preserves that the answer was sincerely meant and contained no lie.
“Wrestling with his choices” preserves the struggle and the long detour.
“The words echoed” naturally carries the persistent inward muttering.
“Ended my enemies’ lives” keeps the lethal result of Sama Pyo’s cruel, sure methods.
SOL retains the hallucination-like voices among the battle’s blood and screams.
SOL preserves familiar faces appearing over the enemies as they collapse.
“The memories” clarifies what rises like mist and passes like wind from the surrounding context.
The source’s darkness is preserved without the baseline’s added intensifier “deep.”
“Buoyed by drink” keeps the sense of her steps and voice being aided by intoxication.
SOL keeps the wet, tearful eyes that the surrounding circumstances could not conceal.
SOL retains the vivid recollection without changing its emphasis.
SOL preserves both the fuss about the moon and his silence at her unexpected question.
“Spoken” naturally renders opening his mouth to speak while retaining her tear-filled eyes.
The source reassures her that it is all right even if she cannot do well; SOL shifts this to the outcome.
SOL naturally preserves the comparison between her eyes, the full moon, and a crescent.
SOL keeps both the unforeseen day and the pitch-black Force rushing toward him.
The source says the rushing sound swallowed the surrounding noise; SOL instead makes it swallow Jeok Cheongang’s shout.
“Even that much reason” preserves the source’s point that he lacked the capacity to react.
SOL keeps the two streams’ murkiness and their seeming lack of life without adding a comparison.
The preceding clause already establishes simultaneity, so SOL removes a redundant connector.
SOL keeps the key image of shattering and gives it natural emphasis.
“Inexplicable” preserves the speaker’s inability to understand what he did.
“So complete” omits the source’s explicit image of a perfect shattering.
“The last two” preserves that only two Black Ghosts remained.
“Crossed” drops the ghostly horse’s leap across the open air.
SOL preserves the blast’s violence and the already-burst eardrums being shaken.
“In its path” naturally preserves that others besides him were where the attackers were headed.
“Tangled” preserves the four streaks becoming intertwined in midair.
SOL keeps the air exploding and the earth overturning under the force.
The tense change does not alter the two superhumans’ rush to save him.
“Pierced and sliced” preserves the weapons’ actions against the Black Ghosts.
SOL reorders the linked actions clearly while preserving the Saints’ exhaustion and the Black Ghosts’ refusal to fall.
The Black Ghosts’ refusal to fall is retained in the preceding SOL hunk.
“After dozens of deaths” preserves their repeated deaths and returns.
SOL preserves the spells’ effects on healing, strength, and speed.
“Closer to their limits than anyone else” is an unsupported comparison; the source says they had reached their deepest limits.
“Fell on my cheek” loses the source’s image of the gaze touching his cheek.
“Supposed to die” keeps the sense that this was not his place to fall.
The thought about the promise is retained in the next SOL hunk, and “opened a path” preserves the leaders’ action.
SOL restores the source’s thought about the unkeepable promise in a complete sentence.
“My greatest memory in this world” naturally preserves the importance of the person and the moment.
SOL preserves the difficult first meeting without imposing a literal “feud.”
The omitted “together” is already conveyed by the two of them falling into step.
Dropping “And” keeps the transition while avoiding a needless connective.
“Being apart no longer felt right” preserves their closeness in natural English.
“When I sent him away” adds the speaker’s agency; the source only says he worried when separated from him.
SOL clearly preserves that he never saw where or by whom Hyuk Mujin died.
SOL preserves the hypothetical miracle and the certainty they would never meet again.
“I would die before it could be” preserves that he would die before the promise could be fulfilled.
The source presents the waiting people as an alternative with “or”; SOL changes that to “and.”
“Without pause” preserves the tireless rekindling of the dying flame.
The source says the blood was spurting upward; SOL changes its physical direction to beneath his feet.
SOL preserves the final, sole path for both the living and the dead.
“Clearly” preserves the blood-red eyes’ perceptibility without adding perfect clarity.
SOL retains the storm of blood and the monster standing beyond it.
“Come to me of your own accord” preserves the taunt that he came voluntarily when he should have fled.
SOL makes clear that the Blood Lord smiled at all three while preserving their positions and exhaustion.
“Now” preserves the transition to the threat of death.
